questions.prompt: What is the capital city of Cyprus?

hints.nudge: A capital city is where a country’s government meets. The other three are capital cities too, of other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Cyprus article.

questions.prompt: Which language is an official language of Cyprus?

hints.nudge: An official language is the one used in schools, courts and government. The other three are spoken in other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Cyprus article.

questions.proof: The official languages are Greek and Turkish.

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “The Turkish Republic of Northern Cyprus (TRNC), a de facto state only recognized by _____ is situated in the north of the island.”

hints.nudge: In the sentence the missing word sits beside “recognized”. It names one thing, not an action.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Cyprus article.

questions.proof: The Turkish Republic of Northern Cyprus (TRNC), a de facto state only recognized by Turkey is situated in the north of the island.

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “Tourism is very important to the country, as tourism made up 23% of its economy in _____.”

hints.nudge: It is a year in the twenty-first century.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Cyprus article.

questions.proof: Tourism is very important to the country, as tourism made up 23% of its economy in 2020.

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “On 1 January _____ Cyprus adopted the Euro, the single European currency.”

hints.nudge: It is a year in the twenty-first century.
hints.whereToLook: It is further down the Cyprus article, under the heading “History”.

questions.proof: On 1 January 2008 Cyprus adopted the Euro, the single European currency.
